newsitem.title: USA: U.S. midcontinent diffs soft as liquidity returns.
newsitem.headline: U.S. midcontinent diffs soft as liquidity returns.

text.p: Spot refined product differentials in the U.S. midcontinent softened Tuesday, particularly in Group Three, after liqudity returned to a market that had been thinly bullish, traders said.

Prompt unleaded gasoline in the Group was heard done at levels as weak as 2.00 cents over June NYMEX after flirting with levels of nearly 3.00 cents over late last week. Any month barrels were bid at the price of the June screen.
Traders said a number of events last week had kept activity to a bare minimum, and now that liquidity was back, talk had turned decisively in favor of outnumbered buyers.
Diesel in the Group was offered about 0.25 cent weaker at 4.75 cents over June NYMEX heat futures, with any month barrels bid at 4.00 cents over.
Differentials in Chicago were more steady than in the Group, but the same bearish flavor could be discerned in that market as well.
-- Oliver Ludwig New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1633
